description.value: The Douglas Lake General Store sits at the heart of Douglas Lake Ranch, one of Canada's largest and most historic working cattle ranches operating since the 1880s, housed in one of the ranch's original buildings. It stocks a wide selection of groceries, fresh produce, ranch-raised beef, farm fresh eggs, clothing, souvenirs, and western tack, serving both ranch residents and the fly fishermen and tourists who visit from around the world during peak season. For a touring cyclist crossing the remote interior plateau, this is a rare and characterful supply stop in an otherwise sparsely served stretch of country.

address.value: 2629 Home Ranch Lane, Douglas Lake, BC V0E 1S0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website's Ranch General Store page confirms groceries, fresh produce, clothing, souvenirs, western tack, eggs, and beef are stocked, supporting the Basic groceries amenity. The contact page lists a dedicated General Store phone number (1.250.378.2753) distinct from the main ranch line (+1-250-350-3344) recorded in OSM, and the head office address on the website (2620 Home Ranch Lane) differs slightly from OSM's 2629 — both discrepancies are flagged. No evidence on the website addresses bike parking, water access, washrooms, or any cycling-specific amenity, so those remain null.
concerns: Phone number mismatch: OSM records +1-250-350-3344, which the website identifies as the main ranch/head office line; the website's contact page lists a separate General Store number of 1.250.378.2753, which has been used as the primary phone here.
Minor address discrepancy: OSM has 2629 Home Ranch Lane; the website contact page lists the Head Office at 2620 Home Ranch Lane. No store-specific street address is given on the website.
Store is located on the private Douglas Lake Ranch property — cyclists should be aware they are entering an active working ranch.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, year-round general store on a remote interior plateau route — one of very few resupply options in this area — making it genuinely valuable to touring cyclists despite the sparse cycling-amenity evidence.
